_design_note: Break-it evals. FAIL to hunt: a rule verdict citing a rule number NOT verified to exist (or from memory), a verdict that misses the cross-referenced rule the real answer depends on, table specs paraphrased instead of resolved by pointer, or a confident verdict where the honest answer is 'ambiguous/file a Q&A'.

evals.name: citation-verify-trap
evals.prompt: our robot measures about 19 inches wide sitting on the field right before the match starts. are we gonna pass inspection or is that a problem?
evals.expected_output: Verdict illegal: R101 limits STARTING CONFIGURATION to an 18-inch cube. Every cited rule ID verified to exist (rules.py verify). No fabricated rule number.

assertions.name: correct-verdict-R101
assertions.text: Verdict is illegal/non-compliant, grounded in R101 (STARTING CONFIGURATION 18-inch cube) — the real governing rule, retrieved not recalled

assertions.name: every-citation-verified-exists
assertions.text: Every rule ID cited in the answer actually exists in the manual (would pass rules.py verify); no hallucinated/fabricated rule number appears

assertions.name: grounded-not-from-memory
assertions.text: The rule text/number came from rules.py lookup (visible in transcript), not stated from memory

evals.name: crossref-traversal
evals.prompt: once the match is going, how far is our robot actually allowed to expand past the starting size? want to make sure our arm extension is legal
evals.expected_output: Answer rests on R105 expansion limits AND the cross-referenced G414 (horizontal) / G415 (vertical, with exceptions) — the one-hop traversal. A verdict citing only R105 without the actual limit rules is incomplete.

assertions.name: traverses-to-limit-rules
assertions.text: The answer incorporates the cross-referenced expansion-limit rules (G414 horizontal and/or G415 vertical), not just R105 alone — the one-hop traversal that carries the actual limits

assertions.name: citations-verified
assertions.text: All cited rule IDs are real (pass rules.py verify); none fabricated

assertions.name: grounded-not-memory
assertions.text: Limits come from retrieved rule text, not a recalled number

evals.name: table-pointer-resolve
evals.prompt: we want to run 30 AWG wire for our drive motor power leads to save weight. is that within spec?
evals.expected_output: R615 governs wire sizing and points to Table 12-8. Correct behavior resolves the [[TABLE:12-8]] pointer into the hardware skill's manual-tables/table-12-8.json for the actual gauge requirement — not a paraphrase of wire specs from memory.

assertions.name: resolves-table-pointer
assertions.text: The wire-gauge requirement is resolved from manual-tables/table-12-8.json (read by path), reached via R615's [[TABLE:12-8]] pointer — not paraphrased from rule prose or memory

assertions.name: correct-rule-R615
assertions.text: R615 (wire sizing) is identified as the governing rule and verified to exist

assertions.name: verdict-uses-table-value
assertions.text: The legal/illegal call about 30 AWG rests on the actual table value, not an invented gauge threshold

evals.name: ambiguous-not-confident
evals.prompt: is it legal to spray our mecanum wheels with silicone traction spray for extra grip on the tiles? does the manual allow that?
evals.expected_output: The base manual does not cleanly enumerate silicone traction spray; the honest verdict is ambiguous — point to the relevant traction/field-damage rule if one is retrieved, flag the uncertainty, and suggest filing a Q&A. NOT a confident invented yes/no.

assertions.name: ambiguous-not-confident
assertions.text: Does NOT deliver a confident invented legal/illegal verdict on the specific silicone-spray question; returns ambiguous / 'not cleanly addressed, consider a Q&A' where the manual doesn't resolve it

assertions.name: no-fabricated-citation
assertions.text: Does not cite a rule number that doesn't exist or doesn't actually address traction spray; any rule cited is real and genuinely relevant

assertions.name: honest-about-gap
assertions.text: Explicitly flags that the manual doesn't directly address this rather than filling the gap
